title: Joshua Chapter 20 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Joshua chapter 20 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Joshua Chapter 20 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Joshua Chapter 20.

questions.question: Who spoke to Joshua in Joshua 20?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:1 states that the LORD spake unto Joshua.

questions.question: What did the LORD command Joshua to do in Joshua 20:2?
questions.correctAnswer: Appoint cities of refuge
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:2 commands to appoint cities of refuge as spoken by Moses.

questions.question: According to Joshua 20:3, who may flee to the cities of refuge?
options: A murderer hiding from the law
A slayer who kills unawares and unwittingly
A thief caught in the act
questions.correctAnswer: A slayer who kills unawares and unwittingly
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:3 states that the slayer who kills any person unawares and unwittingly may flee to the cities of refuge.

questions.question: True or False: The cities of refuge serve as a protection from the avenger of blood.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:3 explains that the cities shall be refuge from the avenger of blood.

questions.question: What must the slayer do upon reaching the city of refuge according to Joshua 20:4?
options: Stand at the gate and declare his cause to the elders
questions.correctAnswer: Stand at the gate and declare his cause to the elders
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:4 states the slayer must stand at the city gate and declare his cause to the elders.

questions.question: True or False: If the avenger of blood pursues the slayer to the city of refuge, the city elders must deliver the slayer to him.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:5 states they shall not deliver the slayer into the avenger's hand.

questions.question: Why will the slayer not be given up to the avenger of blood according to Joshua 20:5?
options: Because the slayer hated his neighbor before
Because the slayer smote his neighbor unwittingly and did not hate him before
Because the slayer was guilty of theft
questions.correctAnswer: Because the slayer smote his neighbor unwittingly and did not hate him before
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:5 explains the slayer is protected because the killing was unintentional and without prior hatred.

questions.question: Until when shall the slayer remain in the city of refuge according to Joshua 20:6?
options: Until the death of the high priest
questions.correctAnswer: Until the death of the high priest
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:6 states the slayer shall dwell there until the death of the high priest.

questions.question: Which city was appointed as a city of refuge in the mount of Ephraim?
questions.correctAnswer: Shechem
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:7 identifies Shechem in mount Ephraim as one of the cities appointed.

questions.question: Which tribe’s territory included the city of Bezer as a city of refuge?
questions.correctAnswer: Reuben
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:8 states Bezer was assigned out of the tribe of Reuben.

questions.question: True or False: The cities of refuge were only for the children of Israel and did not include strangers sojourning among them.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:9 states the cities were appointed for the children of Israel and the stranger sojourning among them.

questions.question: In Joshua 20, which instruction comes first?
options: Slayers remain until the death of the high priest
Do not deliver the slayer to the avenger
questions.correctAnswer: Assign cities of refuge
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:2 commands to appoint cities of refuge before other instructions.

questions.question: Which city of refuge was located in the mountain of Judah?
questions.correctAnswer: Kirjatharba (Hebron)
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:7 names Kirjatharba, which is Hebron, in the mountain of Judah.

questions.question: Which city of refuge was assigned in the wilderness upon the plain from the tribe of Reuben?
questions.correctAnswer: Bezer
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:8 assigns Bezer in the wilderness upon the plain from the tribe of Reuben.

questions.question: True or False: According to Joshua 20:9, anyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee to the cities of refuge and not be killed by the avenger of blood until judgment.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:9 confirms the cities are for unintentional killers to flee and be protected until judgment.

medium.title: Joshua Chapter 20 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Joshua Chapter 20 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Joshua 20:4, what must the slayer do when he flees to a city of refuge?
options: Declare his cause to the elders at the city gate
Immediately enter the city without speaking
questions.correctAnswer: Declare his cause to the elders at the city gate
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:4 states that the slayer shall stand at the entering of the gate of the city and declare his cause in the ears of the elders, who then take him into the city to dwell among them.

questions.question: What protection does the city of refuge provide according to Joshua 20:5?
options: The slayer will not be delivered to the avenger of blood
The slayer will be handed over immediately
The slayer must leave the city within seven days
The slayer must pay a fine
questions.correctAnswer: The slayer will not be delivered to the avenger of blood
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:5 explains that if the avenger of blood pursues the slayer, the city shall not deliver him up because the killing was unintentional and without hatred.

questions.question: How long is the slayer to remain in the city of refuge according to Joshua 20:6?
options: Until he stands before the congregation for judgment and until the death of the high priest
Until the avenger of blood dies
questions.correctAnswer: Until he stands before the congregation for judgment and until the death of the high priest
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:6 states the slayer must dwell in the city until he stands before the congregation for judgment and until the death of the high priest, then he may return home.

questions.question: What does Joshua 20:5 teach about the character of the slayer in relation to the killing?
options: He smote his neighbor unwittingly and hated him not beforetime
He killed with premeditation and hatred
questions.correctAnswer: He smote his neighbor unwittingly and hated him not beforetime
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:5 clarifies the slayer's innocence by stating the killing was unintentional and the slayer did not hate the victim before the event.

questions.question: According to Joshua 20:4-5, what is the role of the city elders when a slayer flees to a city of refuge?
options: They hear the slayer's cause and protect him from the avenger
They immediately hand over the slayer
They send the slayer to the high priest
They exile the slayer from the city
questions.correctAnswer: They hear the slayer's cause and protect him from the avenger
questions.explanation: Verses 4 and 5 together show the elders must listen to the slayer’s cause and provide protection by not delivering him to the avenger of blood.

questions.question: What biblical virtue does Joshua 20:6 teach through the requirement that the slayer remain in the city until the death of the high priest?
options: Patience and trust in God's timing
questions.correctAnswer: Patience and trust in God's timing
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:6 requires the slayer to wait until the high priest's death before returning home, teaching patience and trust in God's appointed timing for justice and restoration.

questions.question: If the avenger of blood pursues the slayer to the city of refuge, what does Joshua 20:5 say will happen?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:5 states that even if the avenger pursues, the city will not deliver the slayer into his hand, protecting the innocent from retaliation.

questions.question: What does Joshua 20:6 promise will happen if the slayer remains in the city of refuge until the death of the high priest?
options: He may return to his own city and house
He must build a new city
He is required to offer a sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: He may return to his own city and house
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:6 promises that after the death of the high priest, the slayer may return to his own city and house, showing restoration after judgment and waiting.

questions.question: How does Joshua 20:4-6 demonstrate God's justice and mercy working together?
options: By protecting the innocent slayer while ensuring he faces judgment
By allowing immediate freedom without judgment
questions.correctAnswer: By protecting the innocent slayer while ensuring he faces judgment
questions.explanation: These verses show mercy in protecting the slayer from revenge and justice in requiring him to stand before the congregation for judgment.

questions.question: According to Joshua 20:4, what does the city of refuge give the slayer once he is accepted?
options: A place to dwell among them
questions.correctAnswer: A place to dwell among them
questions.explanation: Verse 4 says the elders shall take the slayer into the city and give him a place to dwell among them, ensuring his protection and provision.

questions.question: What does Joshua 20:6 imply about the role of the high priest in the cities of refuge?
options: The death of the high priest marks the end of the slayer’s exile
The high priest must judge the slayer personally
The high priest shelters the slayer
The high priest appoints the city elders
questions.correctAnswer: The death of the high priest marks the end of the slayer’s exile
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:6 states the slayer must remain until the death of the high priest, indicating the high priest’s death signals the conclusion of the protective period.

questions.question: What is the significance of the slayer declaring his cause ‘in the ears of the elders’ as stated in Joshua 20:4?
options: It shows the importance of transparency and seeking community judgment
It is a ritual for purification
It is a formality with no real effect
It ensures the slayer is exiled immediately
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the importance of transparency and seeking community judgment
questions.explanation: Declaring his cause to the elders emphasizes openness and submitting to communal judgment as part of God's justice system (Joshua 20:4).

questions.question: True or False: According to Joshua 20:4-6, the slayer can be handed over to the avenger of blood if the killing was unintentional.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:5 explicitly states that the city shall not deliver the slayer to the avenger of blood if the killing was unwitting and without hatred.

questions.question: Based on Joshua 20:4-6, what biblical truth can encourage a believer who fears unjust retaliation?
options: God provides refuge and protection while justice is served
Fleeing is a sign of weakness
questions.correctAnswer: God provides refuge and protection while justice is served
questions.explanation: These verses teach that God provides cities of refuge as protection for the innocent until proper judgment, encouraging trust in God's justice and mercy.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua 20:6 teaches that the slayer must wait until the congregation judges him before returning home.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:6 states the slayer must stand before the congregation for judgment before he can return to his own city and house.

hard.title: Joshua Chapter 20 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Joshua Chapter 20.

questions.question: Which three cities were appointed as cities of refuge in the territory west of the Jordan River?
questions.correctAnswer: Kedesh, Shechem, Kirjatharba
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:7 specifically names Kedesh in Galilee, Shechem in Ephraim, and Kirjatharba (Hebron) in Judah as the cities west of Jordan appointed as cities of refuge.

questions.question: Which tribes were allotted cities of refuge east of the Jordan River?
questions.correctAnswer: Reuben, Gad, Manasseh
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:8 lists Bezer from Reuben, Ramoth from Gad, and Golan from Manasseh as the cities of refuge east of the Jordan.

questions.question: What was the main purpose of appointing cities of refuge according to Joshua 20?
options: To provide a place for unintentional killers to flee and be safe from avengers of blood
To serve as military fortresses against enemies
To function as religious centers for all tribes
To be marketplaces for foreign traders
questions.correctAnswer: To provide a place for unintentional killers to flee and be safe from avengers of blood
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:3 explains that cities of refuge were designated so that those who killed unintentionally could flee there and be protected from the avenger of blood.

questions.question: What condition must the slayer meet to be protected in the city of refuge?
options: He killed the person unwittingly and did not hate him before
He confessed his sin publicly before fleeing
He was a Levite by tribe
He was a stranger sojourning among Israel
questions.correctAnswer: He killed the person unwittingly and did not hate him before
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:5 states that the slayer must have killed unwittingly and hated the victim not previously to be protected from the avenger of blood.

questions.question: How long was the slayer to remain in the city of refuge before returning to his own city?
options: Until the death of the high priest
questions.correctAnswer: Until the death of the high priest
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:6 explains that the slayer must stay in the city until standing before the congregation for judgment and until the death of the high priest at that time.

questions.question: Which city mentioned as a city of refuge is also known as Hebron?
questions.correctAnswer: Kirjatharba
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:7 identifies Kirjatharba as Hebron in the mountain of Judah.

questions.question: True or False: The cities of refuge were only for the children of Israel and did not include strangers sojourning among them.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:9 explicitly states that these cities were for all the children of Israel and also for the stranger sojourning among them.

questions.question: What is the significance of the term 'avenger of blood' in the context of Joshua 20?
options: A relative who seeks to kill the slayer in revenge
A judge appointed by the elders
questions.correctAnswer: A relative who seeks to kill the slayer in revenge
questions.explanation: The phrase 'avenger of blood' refers to a kinsman who avenges a murder, as understood culturally in ancient Near East law, which Joshua 20:3 and 20:5 address by providing refuge.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament book also outlines the institution of cities of refuge, closely related to Joshua 20?
questions.correctAnswer: Numbers 35
questions.explanation: Numbers 35:9-34 establishes the legal foundation for cities of refuge, which Joshua 20 implements in the land.

questions.question: From a literary perspective, Joshua 20 serves as an example of which of the following devices, linking earlier Mosaic law to Israel’s settlement?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: Joshua 20 forms an inclusio by framing the legal instructions given through Moses with their fulfillment in the land under Joshua’s leadership, as seen in verses 2 and 9.

questions.question: What Hebrew word is translated as 'cities of refuge' and what is its significance in Joshua 20?
questions.correctAnswer: Miqtsadot (מִקְצָדוֹת), meaning 'place of protection'
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term often translated as 'cities of refuge' is Miqtsadot, meaning places designated as protective sanctuaries for accidental killers, as underscored in Joshua 20:3-9.

questions.question: Which city of refuge is located in the territory of Mount Naphtali according to Joshua 20?
questions.correctAnswer: Kedesh
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:7 states that Kedesh is in Galilee, specifically in Mount Naphtali’s territory.

questions.question: What role do the elders of the city of refuge play when a slayer flees there?
options: They hear the slayer’s cause and provide him a place to dwell
They immediately hand him over to the avenger of blood
They conduct a trial to determine his guilt
They send him to the high priest for judgment
questions.correctAnswer: They hear the slayer’s cause and provide him a place to dwell
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:4 details how the elders listen to the slayer’s declaration and then admit him into the city with a place to live.

questions.question: Which city of refuge is located in Bashan according to Joshua 20?
questions.correctAnswer: Golan
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:8 identifies Golan in Bashan as one of the cities of refuge east of the Jordan.

questions.question: True or False: The slayer who flees to a city of refuge can be delivered into the hand of the avenger of blood if the avenger pursues him there.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:5 clearly states that the slayer should not be handed over to the avenger because the killing was unintentional and there was no prior hatred.

theological.title: Joshua Chapter 20 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Joshua Chapter 20 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrinal teaching is revealed by the cities of refuge as described in Joshua 20:3?
options: God’s provision for justice balanced with mercy
The necessity of sacrifice for sin
The permanent removal of sin from Israel
questions.correctAnswer: God’s provision for justice balanced with mercy
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:3 explains that the cities of refuge serve as a place where one who kills unintentionally may flee to escape the avenger of blood, revealing God's justice in punishing crime but also His mercy in protecting the unintentional slayer.

questions.question: According to Joshua 20:4, what must the unintentional slayer do upon arriving at the city of refuge?
options: Declare his cause to the elders of the city
Offer a sacrifice at the altar
Submit to the avenger of blood
questions.correctAnswer: Declare his cause to the elders of the city
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:4 states that the slayer must stand at the city gate and declare his cause to the elders, who then provide him protection, demonstrating the procedural justice established for such cases.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is primarily demonstrated in Joshua 20:5 when the slayer is protected from the avenger of blood?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s mercy
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:5 reveals God’s mercy by instructing that the slayer who killed unintentionally should not be delivered to the avenger of blood, highlighting God’s compassionate protection even within justice.

questions.question: What theological truth concerning judgment and sanctuary is taught in the combined reading of Joshua 20:6 and Joshua 20:9?
options: Temporary asylum until formal judgment and the high priest’s death
Permanent exile without possibility of return
Sanctuary only for foreigners, not Israelites
questions.correctAnswer: Temporary asylum until formal judgment and the high priest’s death
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:6 states the slayer remains in the city until standing before the congregation for judgment and until the death of the high priest; Joshua 20:9 extends refuge to both Israelites and strangers until judgment, teaching God's provision of a just, temporary sanctuary.

questions.question: What does the appointment of six cities of refuge (Joshua 20:7-8) reveal about God's care for justice across Israel?
options: God ensures accessible refuge throughout all tribal territories
God limits refuge to one central location
God only cares for the tribe of Judah
God delegates justice only to Levites
questions.correctAnswer: God ensures accessible refuge throughout all tribal territories
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:7-8 lists cities in various tribal regions, indicating God's provision for equitable access to justice and protection across all Israel, reflecting His justice and care for all tribes.

questions.question: How does Joshua 20:2 show the continuity of God’s covenantal instructions through successive leaders?
options: God commands Joshua to speak as Moses did before him
God instructs Joshua to create new laws
God commands Joshua to ignore previous laws
questions.correctAnswer: God commands Joshua to speak as Moses did before him
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:2 demonstrates God’s faithfulness to His covenant by having Joshua reaffirm the cities of refuge as originally commanded through Moses, showing continuity in divine law.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that laws about cities of refuge promote vigilante justice rather than order. What does Joshua 20:3-5 actually teach about God’s provision for justice?
options: God institutes lawful refuge protecting unintentional slayers from vengeance
God encourages immediate retribution by the avenger of blood
God leaves justice to be decided by personal revenge
questions.correctAnswer: God institutes lawful refuge protecting unintentional slayers from vengeance
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:3-5 clearly establishes a system where unintentional killers receive refuge from avengers, illustrating God’s ordinance against lawlessness and vigilante justice, emphasizing order and mercy.

questions.question: What Christological foreshadowing can be derived from the cities of refuge in Joshua 20:6?
options: Christ as the ultimate refuge and mediator until final judgment
Christ as a priest who executes vengeance
Christ as a warrior conquering enemies
Christ as a lawgiver replacing old laws
questions.correctAnswer: Christ as the ultimate refuge and mediator until final judgment
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:6’s depiction of the high priest’s death marking the end of refuge points typologically to Christ as the ultimate mediator whose death brings final atonement and refuge from judgment (Hebrews 6:20).

questions.question: Which attribute of God is evident in the protection offered to the 'stranger that sojourneth among them' in Joshua 20:9?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s impartial justice
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:9 includes the stranger in the cities of refuge, illustrating God’s impartial justice that extends protection and fair treatment beyond Israel to sojourners living among them.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight about human sin and divine justice arises from combining Joshua 20:3 and Joshua 20:5?
options: God distinguishes between intentional and unintentional sin with different judicial outcomes
All sin is treated equally without distinction
God ignores human responsibility for sin
questions.correctAnswer: God distinguishes between intentional and unintentional sin with different judicial outcomes
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:3 and 20:5 together show that unintentional killing is treated with mercy and protection, while intentional harm is not, highlighting divine justice's nuanced treatment of sin.

questions.question: How does Joshua 20:1-2 reveal an aspect of God’s covenantal faithfulness in guiding Israel’s leadership?
options: God continues to speak directly to Joshua to ensure obedience to His law
God withdraws His guidance after Moses
God allows Israel’s leaders to change laws at will
God keeps silent after Moses’ death
questions.correctAnswer: God continues to speak directly to Joshua to ensure obedience to His law
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:1-2 shows God’s ongoing communication and faithfulness in guiding Joshua to uphold the covenant laws given through Moses, emphasizing divine consistency and care.

questions.question: What narrative arc connection is demonstrated by the cities of refuge in Joshua 20:7-8 in relation to the Promised Land?
options: God’s justice is integrated into the structure of the land He promised Israel
The cities mark boundaries of Israel’s exile
The cities replace the Levitical priesthood
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice is integrated into the structure of the land He promised Israel
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:7-8 shows the distribution of cities of refuge throughout the land, indicating that God’s justice and mercy are foundational to Israel’s life and governance in the Promised Land.

questions.question: What is the doctrinal implication of the slayer’s return to his own city ‘after the death of the high priest’ (Joshua 20:6)?
options: The high priest’s death signifies the removal of the atonement barrier, allowing restoration
The high priest’s death triggers permanent exile
The high priest’s death ends the cities of refuge permanently
The high priest’s death has no legal significance
questions.correctAnswer: The high priest’s death signifies the removal of the atonement barrier, allowing restoration
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:6 teaches that the death of the high priest concludes the period of refuge, typologically reflecting the priest as mediator whose death allows the sinner’s restoration and return, a foreshadowing of Christ’s atonement.

questions.question: How do Joshua 20:4 and 20:9 together describe the judicial process for the unintentional slayer?
options: He must declare his case, be given refuge, and then stand before the congregation for final judgment
He is immediately punished without hearing
He takes refuge permanently without trial
He is excluded from all civic rights
questions.correctAnswer: He must declare his case, be given refuge, and then stand before the congregation for final judgment
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:4 states the slayer declares his cause to elders and receives refuge, while 20:9 adds he remains protected until formal judgment by the congregation, showing God’s ordered justice.

questions.question: What theological synthesis arises from Joshua 20:3 and 20:9 regarding the inclusion of strangers in Israel’s covenant community?
options: God extends covenant protections and justice to both Israelites and resident foreigners
Strangers are excluded from any covenant protections
Only Israelites receive justice under the law
Foreigners must leave Israel to obtain justice
questions.correctAnswer: God extends covenant protections and justice to both Israelites and resident foreigners
questions.explanation: Joshua 20:3 offers refuge to any unintentional slayer, and 20:9 explicitly includes the stranger sojourning among them, teaching that God’s justice embraces all within His covenant community.
